transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC (52 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Eli Winters (Redwood CSM), Diane Lopez (Riverbend Head of AI), Benji Ahmed (Platform Eng), Sofia Ramos (Security), Mark Tavares (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Kickoff/handoff from sales to CS; discussed private deployment vs dedicated; security and network checklist; defined pilot scope and success metrics; assigned owners for docs and perf test.

--- Topics / Sections ---
1) Timeline & milestones
2) Network & deployment model (VPC peering / Private)
3) Security / compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO, SSO, KMS)
4) Pilot scope & evals
5) Runbook / fallback

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time today. Quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE, and with me is Connor, our SE, and Eli who will be your CSM through activation.
[00:18] Diane: Thanks, Maya. Hi all, Diane here. We're excited to get the activation started, want to make sure security is checked early.
[00:26] Connor: Hey folks, quick note — we'll focus today on the hands-on bits: network, pilot perf, and what's in the runbook. I might ask for some infra details, Benji.
[00:40] Benji: yep, I have our VPC folks on standby. We currently have a 10.0.0.0/16 backbone for prod and a 10.1.0.0/16 for sandbox.
[00:48] Sofia: And from security, we need answers on audit logs, k-e-m-s — KMS encryption flow, and SSO integration, preferably SAML.
[00:56] Maya: Great, we'll walk through those. Quick question on timeline — what's your target for a limited pilot? Diane?
[01:06] Diane: Ideally mid-April for pilot start, but the realistic window is end of March if we can lock down network and security this week.
[01:15] Mark: We're trying to align pilot with the clinical workflows team; mid-April helps their sprint planning.
[01:23] Connor: Okay good. For the private deployment we have two main patterns: VPC peering into Redwood Private control plane, or PrivateLink style endpoint. Both have tradeoffs on routing and egress logging.
[01:38] Benji: Are there any constraints on peering with multiple accounts? We run across org accounts and need cross-account access.
[01:46] Connor: Yep that's common. We typically recommend a single peering per region and then use route tables for cross-account access, or use PrivateLink to avoid broad peering. We can produce a diagram.
[01:58] Sofia: Also need to confirm that the KV cache and model cache never touch our S3 buckets or that we can manage retention. Logs have to be retained 365 days.
[02:08] Eli: Note — retention requirements will influence what we enable for token-level logs. We can support anonymized logging and point to the retention policy in the onboarding docs.
[02:20] Diane: What about auxiliary data like embeddings — do they persist in any Redwood storage?
[02:26] Connor: For Private we run in your VPC so embeddings don't leave your environment unless you opt into a hosted feature. For Dedicated yes we have options but can disable persistent storage if you want ephemeral caches.
[02:40] Mark: Perf question: what's the expected latency for a 1k token request in your Dedicated vs Private setups?
[02:48] Connor: Ballpark: Dedicated with pinned capacity we see 150-220ms per token depending on model and batch profile; Private depends on infra you attach — with good GPU selection similar ranges, but we should run a baseline test.
[03:02] Benji: Baseline test — can you outline what you need from us? CPU/memory/GPU specs?
[03:10] Connor: We'll bring a perf script. Ideally we get network RTTs, an instance spec for inference nodes, and sample prompts. We'll do a small litmus test to establish token throughput and median latencies.
[03:24] Diane: On compliance — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO certs. Does Redwood provide a package?
[03:31] Maya: Yes, we can share our SOC2 report and ISO attestations under NDA. I'll attach a redacted snapshot to the folder.
[03:40] Sofia: Also need info on key management — can we bring our own KMS?
[03:45] Connor: Yes, BYOK is supported for the Private control plane and for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. There's some config work but it's standard.
[03:55] Diane: Great. For SSO we will require SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[04:00] Eli: We support SAML + SCIM; we'll document the SSO integration steps and sample metadata.
[04:08] Mark: Is there a standard RBAC model we should plan to adapt to?
[04:12] Maya: We provide role templates: admin, developer, analyst. Those map to token scopes; you can customize via the RBAC API.
[04:20] Benji: On network egress, do you require NAT gateways or do you support VPC endpoints?
[04:26] Connor: We prefer PrivateLink endpoints to minimize egress exposure. We'll send the endpoint configuration and security group rules.
[04:34] Diane: Ok let's talk pilot scope — what's a typical minimum viable pilot?
[04:39] Eli: Typically, 2-3 models, a set of 50-100 sample prompts, and a performance baseline plus quality checks. Success metric often is p50 latency < X ms and accuracy/agreement thresholds on evals.
[04:54] Diane: For accuracy we have internal metrics vs clinician judgement — we can provide 100 annotated examples for preliminary model QA.
[05:02] Connor: Perfect — that will help. Also want to confirm the fallback strategy: if Private becomes overloaded, we can automatically route to a hosted Redwood replica with degraded SLAs. Is that acceptable?
[05:16] Mark: We want predictable behavior; auto-fallback is acceptable only if audit logs show routed requests and we get notification.
[05:24] Sofia: We will require an approval gate before any PII leaves our VPC. Make sure fallback doesn't send PII unless we opt in.
[05:33] Maya: Noted — the default policy won't route PII. We'll add explicit guardrails in the routing policy.
[05:41] Benji: Are there any data residency constraints? We need all data to stay in us-east-1 for now.
[05:47] Connor: That's doable — we can pin region and ensure control plane and inference nodes are in us-east-1.
[05:54] Diane: Ok good. Onboarding timeline — what are the immediate next steps we should expect?
[05:59] Maya: We'll send the Private deployment checklist, SOC2 snapshot, and request your network CIDR. Connor will schedule a perf baseline. Eli will open the onboarding folder and invite your team.
[06:12] Mark: Who owns the runbook? We need an ops contact.
[06:16] Eli: I'll take lead on runbook authoring and we'll want your ops lead to review.
[06:22] Diane: We'll assign that after this call.

[06:35] (small cross talk)
[06:50] Connor: Quick technical deep-dive — for model variants we support canary rollouts at the routing layer, and you can pin traffic percentages. We also have built-in prefix KV cash — sorry KV cache — to speed repeated prompts.
[07:06] Benji: KV cash, got it. How do you manage prompt caching TTLs?
[07:11] Connor: Configurable per-route, typical TTLs 5-30 minutes. We'll suggest conservative TTLs for clinical workloads.
[07:20] Sofia: Audit logs — what granularity do you capture? Token-level or request-level? We need request-level with token hashes, and ability to redaction.
[07:32] Connor: We can capture request-level logs with token-level metrics; for security we can hash or redact token content. We'll include examples in the security doc.
[07:43] (pause)
[08:00] Maya: Quick check — does anyone have blockers for the week?
[08:03] Benji: I need to confirm the peering windows with infra — should be 48 hours to get CIDR and peers.
[08:09] Sofia: I need the SOC2 package and KMS steps; otherwise security is blocked.
[08:15] Diane: We've a compliance board meeting Friday; want to have docs before then.
[08:20] Maya: We'll aim to get you the docs by Tuesday EOD.

[08:30] (silence)
[09:00] Connor: About pilot perf — we'll test with a 75/25 read/write mix, 1k token average. We'll generate a synthetic load and measure p50/p95. Any objections?
[09:12] Mark: Sounds fine, but make sure the synthetic prompts mirror the clinical examples — Diane will supply.
[09:19] Diane: yes I'll put together 100 examples and mark where PII appears.
[09:26] Eli: We'll also add quality checks — a small eval harness that compares outputs to your annotated answers and flags regressions.
[09:36] Benji: For rollout, what does the canary process look like if we go live?
[09:41] Connor: Canary is route percentage based, monitor latency and error rates for 1-2 hours, and then promote if healthy. We can set automated rollback thresholds.
[09:51] Sofia: We need to ensure that every rollback/promotion event is logged to your audit stream and that we get an incident ticket.
[09:58] Maya: Affirmative. We can integrate with your ticketing system during the pilot if you want.

[10:15] (background noise, someone typing)
[10:28] Mark: Quick question on cost — do you have an estimate for pilot monthly run costs?
[10:32] Maya: We'll send a rough estimate, but cost depends on tokens/hour, model choice, and caching. Our Optimize toolkit can provide recommendations to lower unit cost.
[10:44] Diane: Can you share a sample cost calc? Like for 100k tokens/day?
[10:48] Maya: Yes, Connor will prepare a sample with quantization options and batching impacts.

[11:02] Connor: Another note — for Private, we recommend quantized model binaries to reduce GPU RAM and cost. We'll propose a quantized profile for your pilot.
[11:12] Benji: Ok good.

[11:30] Eli: Going to the runbook — I propose a simple incident play: degraded perf -> check infra metrics -> scale capacity -> if not resolved switch to hosted fallback with PII guard -> notify stakeholders. We can tailor details.
[11:46] Sofia: That sequence looks fine, just document the notification timing and who gets paged.
[11:51] Eli: Will do.

[12:05] (brief pause)
[12:20] Maya: Alright, let's recap who will do what. I'll send the SOC2 snapshot and Private checklist by Tue. Connor will prepare perf script and a recommended quantization profile. Eli will open onboarding folder and draft the runbook. Diane/Sofia/Benji will supply prompt set, CIDRs, and security requirements.
[12:40] Diane: Confirming timeline — we'll aim to have the artifacts by 2026-03-11 so a pilot can start late March/early April.
[12:50] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[12:54] (silence)
[13:05] Mark: No, thanks, this was useful.
[13:08] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.
[13:12] Diane: Thanks all.
